submitted.rationale: Index 25 (Co 0.19 / Sb 0.81) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0100%. That is about 20× trirutile CoSb2O6 (index 19) and far above the Co-rich spinel region (index 6, which read negative). The Sb-rich end, likely CoSb2O6 plus Sb oxide, looks like where photoactivity peaks.

rejected.reason: Stoichiometric trirutile CoSb2O6: measured EQE only 0.00052%
Co7Sb2O12 spinel region: measured EQE -0.0015%, so no photoanodic response

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so it should form as a single phase near Sb 0.667. MEGNet predicts a 0.37 eV gap, which is likely underestimated for Co d-states. Even taken at face value, a gap that small would still absorb at 2.7 eV. Measuring index 19 (Sb 0.661) samples the stable ternary phase.

Moderate support: MACE puts spinel Co7Sb2O12 near the hull (0.03 eV/atom), so it probably forms around Sb ~0.22. Its MEGNet gap of 1.44 eV (receipt 410fc5f10a33, obtained before the last measurement) means it absorbs at 2.7 eV. Trirutile index 19 had a negligible EQE, so testing this very different Co-rich region is the most useful next measurement.

Mostly uninformative: CoSb2O4 is 0.17 eV/atom above the hull, so the Sb-rich side should be stable CoSb2O6 plus Sb oxide. Only the trirutile side gave a positive EQE, and the GP UCB favours the unexplored Sb-rich end. Measure index 25.
